verses.en: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
verses.pt: E, como se determinou que navegássemos para a Itália, entregaram Paulo e alguns outros presos a um centurião por nome Júlio, da coorte augusta.

verses.en: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.pt: E, embarcando em um navio de Adramítio, que estava prestes a navegar em demanda dos portos pela costa da Ásia, fizemo-nos ao mar, estando conosco Aristarco, macedônio de Tessalônica.

verses.en: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.pt: No dia seguinte chegamos a Sidom, e Júlio, tratando Paulo com bondade, permitiu-lhe ir ver os amigos e receber deles os cuidados necessários.

verses.en: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.pt: Partindo dali, fomos navegando a sotavento de Chipre, porque os ventos eram contrários.

verses.en: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.pt: Tendo atravessado o mar ao longo da Cilícia e Panfília, chegamos a Mirra, na Lícia.

verses.en: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.pt: Ali o centurião achou um navio de Alexandria que navegava para a Itália, e nos fez embarcar nele.

verses.en: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.pt: Navegando vagarosamente por muitos dias, e havendo chegado com dificuldade defronte de Cnido, não nos permitindo o vento ir mais adiante, navegamos a sotavento de Creta, à altura de Salmone;

verses.en: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.pt: e, costeando-a com dificuldade, chegamos a um lugar chamado Bons Portos, perto do qual estava a cidade de Laséia.

verses.en: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.pt: Havendo decorrido muito tempo e tendo-se tornado perigosa a navegação, porque já havia passado o jejum, Paulo os advertia,

verses.en: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.pt: dizendo-lhes: Senhores, vejo que a viagem vai ser com avaria e muita perda não só para a carga e o navio, mas também para as nossas vidas.

verses.en: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.pt: Mas o centurião dava mais crédito ao piloto e ao dono do navio do que às coisas que Paulo dizia.

verses.en: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.pt: E não sendo o porto muito próprio para invernar, os mais deles foram de parecer que daí se fizessem ao mar para ver se de algum modo podiam chegar a Fênice, um porto de Creta que olha para o nordeste e para o sueste, para ali invernar.

verses.en: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.pt: Soprando brandamente o vento sul, e supondo eles terem alcançado o que desejavam, levantaram ferro e iam costeando Creta bem de perto.

verses.en: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
verses.pt: Mas não muito depois desencadeou-se do lado da ilha um tufão de vento chamado euro-aquilão;

verses.en: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
verses.pt: e, sendo arrebatado o navio e não podendo navegar contra o vento, cedemos à sua força e nos deixávamos levar.

verses.en: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.pt: Correndo a sota-vento de uma pequena ilha chamada Clauda, somente a custo pudemos segurar o batel,

verses.en: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.pt: o qual recolheram, usando então os meios disponíveis para cingir o navio; e, temendo que fossem lançados na Sirte, arriaram os aparelhos e se deixavam levar.

verses.en: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
verses.pt: Como fôssemos violentamente açoitados pela tempestade, no dia seguinte começaram a alijar a carga ao mar.

verses.en: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.pt: E ao terceiro dia, com as próprias mãos lançaram os aparelhos do navio.

verses.en: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.pt: Não aparecendo por muitos dia nem sol nem estrelas, e sendo nós ainda batidos por grande tempestade, fugiu-nos afinal toda a esperança de sermos salvos.

verses.en: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
verses.pt: Havendo eles estado muito tempo sem comer, Paulo, pondo-se em pé no meio deles, disse: Senhores, devíeis ter-me ouvido e não ter partido de Creta, para evitar esta avaria e perda.

verses.en: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
verses.pt: E agora vos exorto a que tenhais bom ânimo, pois não se perderá vida alguma entre vós, mas somente o navio.

verses.en: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
verses.pt: Porque esta noite me apareceu um anjo do Deus de quem eu sou e a quem sirvo,

verses.en: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
verses.pt: dizendo: Não temas, Paulo, importa que compareças perante César, e eis que Deus te deu todos os que navegam contigo.

verses.en: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
verses.pt: Portanto, senhores, tende bom ânimo; pois creio em Deus que há de suceder assim como me foi dito.

verses.en: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
verses.pt: Contudo é necessário irmos dar em alguma ilha.

verses.en: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
verses.pt: Quando chegou a décima quarta noite, sendo nós ainda impelidos pela tempestade no mar de Ádria, pela meia-noite, suspeitaram os marinheiros a proximidade de terra;

verses.en: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
verses.pt: e lançando a sonda, acharam vinte braças; passando um pouco mais adiante, e tornando a lançar a sonda, acharam quinze braças.

verses.en: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
verses.pt: Ora, temendo irmos dar em rochedos, lançaram da popa quatro âncoras, e esperaram ansiosos que amanhecesse.

verses.en: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
verses.pt: Procurando, entrementes, os marinheiros fugir do navio, e tendo arriado o batel ao mar sob pretexto de irem lançar âncoras pela proa,

verses.en: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
verses.pt: disse Paulo ao centurião e aos soldados: Se estes não ficarem no navio, não podereis salvar-vos.

verses.en: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
verses.pt: Então os soldados cortaram os cabos do batel e o deixaram cair.

verses.en: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.pt: Enquanto amanhecia, Paulo rogava a todos que comessem alguma coisa, dizendo: É já hoje o décimo quarto dia que esperais e permaneceis em jejum, não havendo provado coisa alguma.

verses.en: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
verses.pt: Rogo-vos, portanto, que comais alguma coisa, porque disso depende a vossa segurança; porque nem um cabelo cairá da cabeça de qualquer de vós.

verses.en: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
verses.pt: E, havendo dito isto, tomou o pão, deu graças a Deus na presença de todos e, partindo-o começou a comer.

verses.en: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
verses.pt: Então todos cobraram ânimo e se puseram também a comer.

verses.en: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
verses.pt: Éramos ao todo no navio duzentas e setenta e seis almas.

verses.en: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
verses.pt: Depois de saciados com a comida, começaram a aliviar o navio, alijando o trigo no mar.

verses.en: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
verses.pt: Quando amanheceu, não reconheciam a terra; divisavam, porém, uma enseada com uma praia, e consultavam se poderiam nela encalhar o navio.

verses.en: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
verses.pt: Soltando as âncoras, deixaram-nas no mar, largando ao mesmo tempo as amarras do leme; e, içando ao vento a vela da proa, dirigiram-se para a praia.

verses.en: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
verses.pt: Dando, porém, num lugar onde duas correntes se encontravam, encalharam o navio; e a proa, encravando-se, ficou imóvel, mas a popa se desfazia com a força das ondas.

verses.en: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
verses.pt: Então o parecer dos soldados era que matassem os presos para que nenhum deles fugisse, escapando a nado.

verses.en: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
verses.pt: Mas o centurião, querendo salvar a Paulo, estorvou-lhes este intento; e mandou que os que pudessem nadar fossem os primeiros a lançar-se ao mar e alcançar a terra;

verses.en: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
verses.pt: e que os demais se salvassem, uns em tábuas e outros em quaisquer destroços do navio. Assim chegaram todos à terra salvos.
